**Build log, MCP Server Step 2: The MCP module and the two transports** (Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-23).

**What was built.**

- `src/Mcp.js` (new, 258 lines): the protocol over the definition, no transport in it, no library. `Mcp( { Operations, Store, Authorize } )` answers `Tools()` (every operation as `{ name, description, inputSchema }`, the parameters' types and required fields from the definition, `Project` described as an id or a name) and `Handle( Message, Participant )`: `initialize` (the protocol version 2025-06-18, or the client's when it is one of the three we know; the tools capability; the server's name and version), `notifications/initialized`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`; an unknown method -32601, an unknown tool -32602, a message that is no request -32600, an operation that throws -32603; a notification answers nothing; a batch is answered as an array. A call resolves a project given by name to its id (through the store), asks the transport's `Authorize` first, performs the operation as the participant, and answers its JSON as text (an Answer's body as it is, so a report comes as its page); a Refusal is an error result (`isError`) with the sentence and its extras.
- `src/Api.js`: the network transport, `POST /api/mcp`, registered before the JSON body parser with a text body of its own, so a body that is not JSON is answered the protocol's way (-32700); identify and authorize on it as on every route; a notification (or a batch of them) answers 202 with nothing; `GET /api/mcp` and the rest answer 405 with `Allow: POST`. The authorize middleware is now a function, `check( participant, method, path, body, query )`, which the middleware calls for a request and `authorize_operation` calls for each tool call with the operation's route built from its arguments (`Operations.Route`), so a Watcher's `reply` over MCP is refused as it is over REST, by the same rule. `src/Roles.js`: `POST /mcp` is open to every identified caller; each operation is checked on its own action inside.
- `bin/mcp.js` (new, 279 lines; `consensus-mcp` in `package.json`'s bin): the stdio relay. `--server` an address or the Name of a saved server in the global config's Servers list (`--config` the folder, `~/.consensus` by default; the entry's Url and, when it has them, Token and Service); `--service` the header (`MCP` when neither it nor `--token` is given); `--token` an account's token; `--project` fills in `Project` for a tool call that takes one and leaves it out, the tools asked of the server once. One line in, one line out, stderr for anything else; a line that is not JSON is -32700 on the spot; a server that does not answer (or answers 401) is a -32000 error for a request, a note on stderr for a notification; the process ends when stdin does, stdout flushed. It identifies nobody and holds no state.
- `src/Operations.js`: `PARAM_NAMES`, `Route( Operation, Arguments )` (the operation's HTTP request for a client: the path filled from the arguments, the rest as the query or the body) and `Definition()` (the list with no store behind it).
- `src/Tools.js`: the local model's Consensus tools are the definition in Ollama's form. Six reading operations at every level (`list_projects`, `read_plan`, `list_threads`, `list_revisions`, `read_revision`, `waiting`) and seven writing ones when the task's Writes is not none (`thread`, `reply`, `reanchor`, `apply`, `write_text`, `set_state`, `create_plan`), each named, described and typed as the definition says, with `Project` never asked (fixed to the run's), a plan named checked to be the project's, `Revision` supplied for `apply` and `write_text` when left out, `Anchor` taken as plain words, `waiting` narrowed by `Plan`. Each call is the operation's own route over the API as the run (`Operations.Route`), its answer rendered as text for the model (the trees, the plans and the threads as lines, a write as a sentence). What changed for a local model: the tool names are the operation names, so `list_project` is `list_projects`, `read_document` is `read_plan` (which reads a document too), and the plan argument is `Id` as the definition names it; `src/Runner.js`'s hint says so. The file tools are untouched.
- Tests: `test/Mcp.test.js` (new, six tests): the protocol over a fake definition (initialize, the notification, ping, tools/list's schema, tools/call as the participant, the Refusal with its extras, the Answer, the project by name, the transport's authorize refusing before the operation runs, the four errors, the batch); the network transport on a server started in the test (initialize, 202 for the notification, every operation listed, a project by name, a plan and a thread made through the protocol carrying the byline `Relay`, a refusal as an error result, the report as its page, a batch, the parse error, 405, an unknown token refused); the relay over pipes (`bin/mcp.js` spawned: initialize, a plan created with `--project` filled in and the byline `Claude-CLI`, the parse error, ping; a saved server by name from a config folder of the test's; a name no server has; a port nothing listens on; no arguments). `test/Tools.test.js` brought to the names and `Id`; `test/Operations.test.js` unchanged.

**How it was tested.** `node --test`: 252 tests (six more), 248 pass, 3 skipped, one failure: the Work options test's first request, "fetch failed", the race already noted in Step 1's log, now understood: `test/support/Repo.js` runs nine synchronous git commands before that test's first call, blocking the event loop for seconds, so the in-process server's five-second keep-alive timer fires the instant the loop unblocks, as the test's next request goes out on the idle socket. It is the test's, not the move's; a fix (`Connection: close` in the test's request helper, or a longer keep-alive in the test server) is a line, left for your word. The operations, MCP, tools and roles tests together: 21 of 21 on the first run. `test/Api.test.js` run whole four times on this code and four times on Step 1's commit, with nothing else running: eight of eight pass (an earlier four-run on this code failed twice on a run-timing assertion while probe scripts of mine ran alongside; without that load it does not recur, on either code). Nothing is committed.
